i6-block-single.comment: Single-line I6 block: #i6 { i6code }. MUST be tried before the multi-line i6-block rule so an inline closing } isn't mistaken for the start of an unclosed block (which would swallow the rest of the file until an accidental same-indent }). Mirrors emitter-body-single vs emitter-body-multi. [^}\n]* forbids nested braces + newlines, so a genuinely multi-line #i6 { falls through to i6-block. Case-insensitive.

i6-block.comment: Raw Inform 6 block: #i6 { ... } spanning multiple lines. The `\{[^\n}]*$` tail requires the opening brace to be the LAST significant thing on the line (no inline closing }), so an inline `#i6 { code }` does NOT match here and falls to i6-block-single instead. Without this guard `^(\s*)#i6` starts at column 0 and out-competes i6-block-single (which starts at the #) on the earliest-match rule, reopening the swallow-to-EOF bug where the indent-anchored end `^\1}` is never found. Mirrors emitter-body-multi. Captures leading whitespace in group 1 so the end pattern can require the closing } at the same indentation level. Case-insensitive — Beguile lexer is case-insensitive.
i6-block.name: meta.embedded.block.i6.beguile

i6-line.comment: Single-line #i6 directive: #i6 i6code (no braces — parser reads to end of line). Negative lookahead ensures the block form #i6 { is handled by i6-block instead. Case-insensitive.

emitter-body-single.comment: Single-line emitter body: emitter TYPE NAME(params) { i6expr }. Must match before multi-line rule. Case-insensitive.

emitter-body-multi.comment: Multi-line emitter body. Indentation back-reference ensures } matches opener's indent level. Case-insensitive.

interpolated-strings.comment: Interpolated string literal: $"text {expr} text". Outer rule has no name so {expr} spans inherit code colors, not string color.

patterns.comment: Interpolated expression span: { ... }. Negative lookbehind prevents \{ escape from triggering.
patterns.name: meta.interpolation.beguile

patterns.comment: Escape sequences. Dual scope includes string.* so VSCode bracket-pair colorizer ignores { here.
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.interpolated.beguile constant.character.escape.beguile

patterns.comment: Literal string content between interpolation spans
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.interpolated.beguile

dictionary-words.comment: Dictionary word literals: ..word (plural) or .word (singular). Negative lookbehind prevents matching member access on identifiers. Scope prefix is string.unquoted so themes color them in the string bucket by default; the .dictionary-word.beguile suffix lets users target dict words specifically in overrides.

emitter-vars.comment: Substitution placeholders inside emitter bodies: $self, $prop, $target, $class, $counter, $element, $array, or any $identifier (incl. $<paramname>)
emitter-vars.name: variable.language.self.beguile

preprocessor.comment: All preprocessor directive matches are case-insensitive (Beguile lexer is case-insensitive — see project_beguile_case_insensitive memory).

patterns.comment: #define NAME — value portion is left unscoped so the main grammar colors numbers/strings/identifiers naturally (matches C/C++/C# behavior). Case-insensitive.
patterns.name: meta.preprocessor.define.beguile

patterns.comment: I6-level compile-time conditionals: ##ifdef / ##ifndef / ##else / ##endif (and ##if inside emitter bodies). The `##` prefix marks a Beguile transpiler-evaluated conditional (bglParserDirectives.cpp). MUST precede the single-# conditional rule below: without it, `##endif`'s leading # is left unscoped and its inner `#endif` matches the single-# rule (leading # white, rest purple). Longer alternatives (ifdef/ifndef) listed before `if` so `if` can't shadow them. Case-insensitive.
patterns.name: meta.preprocessor.conditional.beguile

patterns.comment: #if / #elif / #else / #endif conditional compilation — condition expression is left unscoped so the main grammar colors identifiers naturally (matches C/C++/C# behavior). Case-insensitive.
patterns.name: meta.preprocessor.conditional.beguile

patterns.comment: #beguilerSettings block header or property reference (#beguilerSettings.propName). Case-insensitive.
patterns.name: keyword.control.directive.beguile

patterns.comment: #i6replace RoutineName [SavedName]; — emits I6 `Replace RoutineName [SavedName];` hoisted above all includes (spec §15.5.1). Unlike bare `#i6 replace X;` (raw-I6-to-EOL, handled by i6-line), this is a structured directive: the operands are ordinary I6 routine identifiers and the statement ends at `;`, so a trailing `// comment` is a genuine Beguile comment. Routine names colored as function entities. Must not use `#i6\b` before this — `#i6replace` has no word boundary after `#i6`. Case-insensitive.

verb-extend-members.comment: Contextual member keywords inside verb-extend bodies: `synonyms`, `grammar`, and `priority` used as statement assignment targets (`synonyms = { }`, `grammar += { }`, `priority = N`). Referenced ONLY from the extend-body rules, so it never fires on an ordinary variable named `priority`/`synonyms` elsewhere in the file. `grammar` also matches keywords-type-declaration (storage.type) globally; re-asserting storage.type here keeps the trio visually consistent (and matches how `grammar` already colors in verb-declaration bodies). Lookahead requires a following `=`, `+=`, or `{` so a bare mention isn't recolored. Case-insensitive — Beguile lexer is case-insensitive.

extend-body-single.comment: Single-line extend body: `extend Name { ... }`. MUST be tried before the multi-line extend-body rule so an inline closing } isn't mistaken for the start of an unclosed block (mirrors i6-block-single vs i6-block). Applies verb-extend member-keyword highlighting to the brace body. Case-insensitive.

extend-body.comment: Multi-line `extend Name { ... }` body. `extend` is global-context, so the closing } aligns with the opener's indentation — the `^\1}` end mirrors i6-block. The begin ends at the opening { and lets the inner patterns (verb-extend member keywords + $self) tokenize the rest; genuine single-line extends are consumed by extend-body-single first, so only true multi-line openers reach here. Worst case on unconventional indentation is an early end (contextual highlighting stops a few lines short), never a swallow-to-EOF. Case-insensitive.

grammar-token-calls.comment: Parameterized grammar tokens: NOUN(Routine) and SCOPE(Routine). Case-insensitive (Beguile lexer is case-insensitive — see project_beguile_case_insensitive memory).

grammar-tokens.comment: Built-in grammar pattern tokens (bare, non-parameterized) — values of the grammarToken enum in beguiLib/bindings/i6StandardLibrary.bgl. `reverse` is the action-target modifier (must be last in a pattern). Case-insensitive. NOTE: this list must be kept in sync with the grammarToken enum; the LSP completion path (lspServer.cpp Phase 1.5) reads the enum directly and does not drift.
grammar-tokens.name: support.constant.grammar-token.beguile

keywords-control.comment: Case-insensitive — Beguile lexer lowercases all identifiers (see project_beguile_case_insensitive memory).
keywords-control.name: keyword.control.beguile

function-definition.comment: Highlight function/method name in definitions: returnType functionName(

patterns.comment: operator keyword in operator declarations (operator ?, operator switch, etc.)
